Q: Convert a date string from Y/m/d format to d/m/Y with PHP A:

use date function

    date('d/M/Y', date_of_birth)

instead of date_format(). Use date()

    <?php echo isset($form_data["db_name"]) ? $form_data["db_name"]->date('d/M/Y',strtotime(date_of_birth)) : ""; ?>"

Q: Render HTML elements simultaneously A:

Nothing drastically different comes to mind. Variations of your ideas include:

  • Put both elements inside a parent and show/hide the parent instead of individual children.

  • Use opacity: 0 / opacity: 1 with transitions: Can make them appear together smoothly.

  • Use document.write (rare, not recommended) or innerHTML in JS to inject multiple elements simultaneously.

Q: Windows batch file - Concatenate all files in subdirectories A: 
@ECHO OFF
REM ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

REM Config:

SET OutFile="T:\Dat2\CombineAllTxt\Out1.txt"

SET RootDir="C:\Dat"
SET RootDrive=C:
SET FilePattern="*.prj"

REM ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

REM Kill OutFile

IF EXIST %OutFile% DEL %OutFile%

REM ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
REM Loop Files incl SubDirs // Variable in Batch-Loop must be Percent + Percent + One Letter

FOR /R %RootDir% %%F in (%FilePattern%) DO (
    ECHO "%%F"
    TYPE "%%F" >>%OutFile%
)

REM ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

PAUSE
